t: Except as provided for in section 101(b)(2), amounts made available under section 101 of this division for civilian personnel compensation and benefits in each department and agency may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to avoid furloughs within such department or agency, consistent with enacted appropriations for fiscal year 2006, except that such authority provided under this section shall not be used until after the department or agency has taken all necessary actions to reduce or defer non-personnel-related administrative expenses.

fable.w: This is a continuing-resolution appropriations provision governing how funds for civilian personnel compensation may be apportioned to avoid furloughs. The only actors are federal departments and agencies managing their own expenses; no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any decision. The phrase "all necessary actions" might sound procedural, but it refers to internal cost-cutting, not to any process that crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to avoid furloughs within such department or agency

qwen_block.w: This section describes internal budgetary procedures for federal agencies regarding the apportionment of funds to avoid furloughs. It involves only federal departments and agencies (inside the government) and does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_block.s: Except as provided for in section 101(b)(2), amounts made available under section 101 of this division for civilian personnel compensation and benefits in each department and agency may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to avoid furloughs within such department or agency, consistent with enacted appropriations for fiscal year 2006, except that such authority provided under this section shall not be used until after the department or agency has taken all necessary actions to reduce or defer non-personnel-related administrative expenses.

opus.w: This section only lets federal departments and agencies apportion appropriated funds for civilian personnel pay at a rate that avoids furloughs, once they have cut non-personnel administrative expenses. It provides for no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Words like "actions" and "department or agency" are just about budget management, so there is no participation.
opus.b: A reader might be tempted by "taken all necessary actions" or by the mention of "department or agency," but neither involves anyone outside the government. The section is a funding provision in a continuing resolution. It lets agencies apportion money for personnel pay faster to avoid furloughs, after they first cut administrative costs. Only federal agencies and their own budgets are involved.

It involves only federal departments and agencies, which are inside the federal government. There is no requirement or recommendation for consultation with outside parties, such as the public, states, or non-federal experts.
qwen_chat.s: Except as provided for in section 101(b)(2), amounts made available under section 101 of this division for civilian personnel compensation and benefits in each department and agency may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to avoid furloughs within such department or agency, consistent with enacted appropriations for fiscal year 2006, except that such authority provided under this section shall not be used until after the department or agency has taken all necessary actions to reduce or defer non-personnel-related administrative expenses.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "operations necessary to avoid furloughs" implies a consultation with employees or unions to determine what is necessary. However, the text does not mandate any such consultation; it merely sets a limit on apportionment based on operational necessity as determined by the agency. The actors involved are federal departments and agencies (inside the government). There is no mention of outside parties, public comment, hearings, or advisory boards with non-federal members.
